Aftermath of the Via D'Amelio bombing in which an anti-mafia judge and 5 bodyguards were blown up by a bomb triggered when the judge rang his mother's doorbell. Palermo, Italy. 1992

The via D'Amelio bombing was a terrorist bombing that took place in Palermo, Sicily, on July 19,1992. It claimed the life of anti-mafia magistrate Paolo Borsellino and five members of his police escort. The bomb, containing some 100 kg of TNT, had been placed in a Fiat 126 parked in front of the house. Normal procedure when Borsellino traveled was to clear the road of cars before his arrival, but this was not allowed by the administration of Palermo,

The so-called agenda rossa, the red notebook in which Borsellino used to write down details of his investigations and which he always carried on his person, disappeared from the site in the moments after the explosion. Agents of the SISDE, Italy's civil intelligence service, were implicated in the massacre and several members of the Sicilian mafia were later convicted for the attack.

I'm referring to [Arduino.cc](https://forum.arduino.cc/) and [Arduino.org](http://www.arduino.org/forums). Most makers and tinkerers know about the big arduino split and the resulting legal battle over the Arduino name. On the face of it there's no real difference aside from the boards with Arduino.org clearly holding a larger selection.

However, when you look at the *community* via the forum numbers you'll see that Arduino.org (the newcomer, started by Arduino co-founder Gianluca Martino) simply doesn't have community support. Here are the numbers as i saw them when i checked:

| Arduino.cc | Arduino.org ---------|----------|--------- Number of user's currently online | 91 | 2 Most users at once | 4125 | 10 Number of forum post's | 2,759,761 | 2620 Total number of user's | 421,435 | 701

######*numbers as of July 20th, 2016 - 8:25 pm. ######**all user number's include myself.

What's more, Arduino.org doesn't seem to release schematics or Eagle Files, even for the old boards already in the public domain. It's clear that they dont hold to the same values that made Arduino so popular in the first place, so does anyone see a reason to use these boards besides novelty and variety?
